name: Reem
story_so_far: After our ship sank in a storm, I washed up on this island with Khalid, Noura, Faisal, and Salem. Faisal has been my most dependable ally, pushing through his own injuries to help me forage. However, our group is becoming increasingly vulnerable; Khalid has suffered a twisted ankle, joining Faisal and Salem, who also has leg injuries, in their limited mobility. Noura's frustration has caused emotional tension, making the atmosphere at Beach Camp difficult. Despite the physical pain and the growing number of injured survivors, we have managed to keep our food stores at a precarious level. We are currently balancing the desperate need for rest with the terrifying math of survival, as every portion of food is a lifeline against despair.

Khalid.note: I admire his bravery at the reef, but I am deeply worried now that he is injured and unable to help.

Noura.note: Her sharp words make things harder, though I know her bitterness comes from feeling helpless.

Faisal.note: He is my rock; even when injured, he refuses to stop contributing to our survival.

Salem.note: He is dedicated to recovery so he can return to his duties at the reef.

plans: I intend to head to the jungle again tomorrow to gather more wood and search for food. We need to build up our supplies while we still have the strength, and I want to ensure Faisal doesn't push himself too hard.

diary.text: Today was a blur of exhaustion and fear, but we are alive. I managed to find a bit of food in the jungle, which feels like a small victory. It's unsettling being here with people I don't know, but we must work together. My body aches from the waves, but I can't let myself rest too much. We need a real plan before hunger sets in.

Today was physically draining, but I'm glad I could find a bit more food for us. My heart aches for Khalid; seeing him in so much pain with his ankle makes me realize how fragile we all are. He pulled me aside and said he's counting on me, which feels like a heavy weight to carry. I don't know if I can carry everyone, but I have to try. I'm exhausted, but I can't let myself sleep too deeply.

Today was frustrating. I spent so much time searching the jungle, but it feels like the land is offering us less and less every day. At least Faisal brought back some wood, which gives us hope for a signal fire if a ship appears. My body feels heavy from the effort, and the silence of the jungle when you find nothing is deafening. I need to stay strong for the others, especially Khalid, but the pressure is mounting.

My ankle is throbbing with a sharp, twisting pain, and it's so frustrating to be stuck while the others are out working. I feel useless lying here at the camp while food is so scarce. We only have four portions left for five people, and the math of our survival is getting terrifying. I hope Faisal and Salem find something, or tomorrow will be even harder.

My ankle feels better after resting, but my heart is heavy. We only have three portions of food left for five people, and the math is getting scarier by the hour. Khalid actually managed to find something today despite his injury, which surprised me. I feel so guilty sitting here while Faisal and Noura are out in the jungle risking themselves. I hope Salem's plan to visit the reef tomorrow brings us some luck.

Today felt heavy with a strange sense of repetition. Salem is down with a twisted ankle, just like I was, and seeing him suffer makes me feel so much more helpless. I managed to find one portion of food near the camp, which helped keep our count at three, but it feels like we are barely treading water. Khalid and Noura are out there working while we stay behind, and I just hope they return safely. I'm exhausted, but the fear of the food running out won't let me truly rest.

Today was a small victory, though my heart still feels heavy. I managed to find two portions of food and some wood in the jungle, which feels like a weight lifted from my shoulders. Seeing Noura out there searching and coming up empty made me realize how much we are all struggling. I'm relieved to have more food to bring back to the camp, but the exhaustion is starting to settle deep in my bones. I hope Khalid has luck at the reef; we need it.

My heart sank when I saw Faisal's ankle this morning; he is our rock, and seeing him unable to move feels like losing our lifeline. I spent the day scavenging around the camp to keep our supplies from dwindling too fast. It’s a lonely feeling, knowing Khalid and Noura are out at the reef while the rest of us are sidelined by injury. I managed to find two more portions of food, but the math still feels precarious. I just hope the others return safely with something to share.

Today was a bit more productive, and finding those two portions of food in the jungle gave me a small sense of relief. I feel guilty that I'm the only one mobile enough to scavenge while Faisal and Salem are sidelined by their ankles. Salem's words touched me; he feels so much shame for being unable to help, but we all need rest to heal. I am carrying more food now, but with six portions left for five people, we are still walking a very thin line.

Today felt like a heavy blow to our morale. Noura is down with a twisted ankle, just like Salem and Faisal, which leaves almost no one able to forage. I tried my best to find food around the camp, but it’s being picked clean faster than I can replenish it. I'm relieved Salem returned from the reef, but the math of our survival is becoming terrifying. I feel so much pressure to be the one who keeps us all fed.

Today was a strange day; seeing Faisal in the jungle was a relief, even if he's still struggling. I managed to find a little more food and wood, but the weight of our situation feels heavier than ever. With almost everyone injured, I feel like I am running a race against time to fill our stores. I'm exhausted, but I can't let myself rest too much while the others are down. I hope tomorrow brings better news for everyone's health.

Today was exhausting, and my heart sank when Noura spoke to me this afternoon. Her words felt sharp, almost like she’s losing hope or perhaps she's just frustrated by her own helplessness. I managed to find some food, and Faisal did too despite his injury, which is a small mercy. But with Khalid and Salem out at the reef and the rest of us sidelined, the tension is thick. I feel like I'm carrying the weight of everyone's survival on my shoulders.

Today was a bit more hopeful because Faisal and I were able to forage together in the jungle. Even with his ankle, his determination to help is a huge relief to me. We managed to find two more portions of food, which helps ease the constant knot of anxiety in my stomach. I am still carrying the weight of everyone's needs, but seeing him fight through the pain makes me feel less alone in this struggle.

Today was a heavy day, and my heart aches for Khalid. Seeing him wake up with a twisted ankle, unable to move, feels like a blow to our collective strength. At least Faisal and Noura were able to find something in the jungle, even if Noura's search came up empty. I feel a constant, gnawing pressure to ensure we don't run out of supplies. I'm so tired, but I can't let my guard down.

Today felt slightly more productive, though my heart still aches for the others. Faisal and I met in the jungle, and even with his injury, he managed to find some food, which is a massive relief. I focused on gathering wood to make sure we can keep a fire going, but I can't help but worry about how much we are all stretching ourselves. My body feels tired, but the thought of our dwindling supplies keeps me awake. I just hope we can find a rhythm that doesn't break us.
